crop.notes: Starts mid-sentence ('stopped at the end of the seventh round by the militia'). The '[Associated Press Report.] The Fight Stopped. Cincinnati, Sept. 7.—The fight was' opening sits at the foot of the previous column. Bottom is complete through 'Allen Arrested'.

title.suggested: Associated Press Report of the Allen-Goss Fight

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Evening Dispatch printed the Associated Press account of the Allen-Goss fight near Walton, Kentucky, stopped by militia and resumed in Boone County, where Goss won on a foul in the 21st round. Allen was arrested at Newport.

metadata.notes: Masthead: St. Louis Dispatch, Thursday Evening, September 7, 1876. Predates the 1878 Post-Dispatch merger.

facts.fact: Allen and Joe Goss fought at Cloverfield near Walton, Kentucky, on the Louisville Short Line about eighteen miles from Cincinnati, before a crowd of about 500
The Covington Light Guards stopped the fight after seven rounds; referee Eph Holland halted it on the advice of the governor's aide, and a second ring was formed below Walton in Boone County
Goss was awarded the fight on a foul in the 21st round, when Allen struck him while he was on his knees, at 11:50 a.m. after 1 hour 52 minutes; Goss was terribly beaten and Allen nearly unmarked
Allen was arrested at Newport, Kentucky, when the trains from the fight arrived there

notes: Recrop to take in the opening lines at the foot of the previous column. The AP gives the start as 7:35; the Dispatch correspondent (573) gives 6:40.
